PS3:pixeljunk-racers.d: PixelJunk Racers is a racing video game developed and published by Q-Games for the PlayStation 3. It was released on the PlayStation Store in 2007 as the first title in the PixelJunk series, a collaboration between Q-Games and Sony Computer Entertainment, who released the game outside Japan. An updated version, PixelJunk Racers: 2nd Lap, was released in 2010.

PS3:weekly-toro-station.d: Doko Demo Issyo (どこでもいっしょ; lit. "Together Everywhere") is a Japanese video game series primarily developed by BeXide Inc. (formerly Bomber eXpress) and published by Sony Interactive Entertainment. The first game was released for the PlayStation in 1999.

PS4:moving-out-2.d: Moving Out 2 is a 2023 cooperative simulation game developed by SMG Studio and DevM Games and published by Team17. It is a sequel to Moving Out. Players attempt to move objects across various levels without hitting objections. It combines elements of strategy, puzzle, and party video games.

PS5:lego-horizon-adventures.d: Lego Horizon Adventures is a 2024 action-adventure game co-developed by Guerrilla Games and Studio Gobo in association with The Lego Group, and published by Sony Interactive Entertainment. It is a spin-off in the Horizon franchise and reinterprets the events of Horizon Zero Dawn (2017) in a Lego-themed environment. The game is played from a fixed isometric perspective and allows the player to control one of four protagonists—Aloy, Varl, Erend, or Teersa—as they battle a rogue artificial intelligence known as HADES, and a sun-worshipping cult led by Helis. The gameplay features a mix of linear platforming and combat that incorporates the franchise's weak-point targeting system.

PS5:pantsu-hunter-back-to-90s.d: Pantsu Hunter: Back to the 90s is an adventure game for the PlayStation 5 in 2019.

Xbox:san-francisco-rush-2049.d: San Francisco Rush 2049 is a 1999 racing video game developed and published by Atari Games for arcades. It was later ported to home systems. It is the third game in the Rush series as the sequel to San Francisco Rush: Extreme Racing and Rush 2: Extreme Racing USA as well as the last to be set in the city of San Francisco. An updated version with fixes and more tracks was later released subtitled Tournament Edition.

XSX:ghostbusters-spirits-unleashed.d: Ghostbusters: Spirits Unleashed is a 2022 asymmetrical action game developed and published by IllFonic. Based on the Ghostbusters franchise, it is set after the events of the 2021 film Ghostbusters: Afterlife and focuses on players tackling matches either as a ghostbuster trying to capture ghosts, or a ghost trying to haunt a location. It was released for Microsoft Windows, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Xbox One and Xbox Series X/S in October 2022. A Nintendo Switch port was released on October 19, 2023.

Switch:gekido-advance-kintaros-revenge.d: Gekido Advance: Kintaro's Revenge is a beat 'em up game for the Game Boy Advance, created by Italian studio NAPS Team. It is a sequel to the PlayStation game Gekido. Unlike the previous installment, this game centers on one protagonist, instead of multiple characters as seen in Gekido. A version for N-Gage was planned but never released.

Switch:tiny-tales-heart-of-forest.d: Tiny Tales: Heart of the Forest is a hidden object game for the Nintendo Switch, developed by Brave Giant and published by Artifex Mundi in 2017.

GB:boulder-dash.d: Boulder Dash is a maze-based puzzle video game released in 1984 by First Star Software for Atari 8-bit computers. It was created by Canadian developers Peter Liepa and Chris Gray. The player controls Rockford, who tunnels through dirt to collect diamonds. Boulders and other objects remain fixed until the dirt beneath them is removed, then they fall and become a hazard.

GBA:tiny-toon-adventures-scary-dreams.d: Tiny Toon Adventures: Scary Dreams is a fighting game for the Game Boy Advance, developed by Treasure and published by Swing! Entertainment.

GBA:yie-ar-kung-fu.d: Yie Ar Kung-Fu is a fighting game developed and published by Konami for arcades. It first had a limited Japanese release in October 1984, before having a wide release nationwide in January 1985 and then internationally in March. Along with Data East's Karate Champ (1984), which influenced Yie Ar Kung-Fu, it is one of the games that established the basis for modern fighting games. The game was inspired by Bruce Lee's Hong Kong martial arts films, with the main player character Oolong modelled after Lee (like Bruceploitation films).

Characters from The Adventures of Jimmy Neutron, Boy Genius, Danny Phantom, SpongeBob SquarePants, Invader Zim, and Tak and the Power of Juju appear. The original developers of the previous games for consoles, Blue Tongue Entertainment, did not return to create this installment.

Linux:space-station-14.d: Space Station 13, often shortened to SS13, is a free-to-play role-playing multiplayer video game originally developed by Exadv1. It runs on the freeware BYOND game engine, originally released in 2003. Sessions in SS13 are round-based; players perform their assigned jobs from a top-down perspective aboard a futuristic space station, co-operating and responding to various player- and environmentally-created events in an attempt to belay a round-ending catastrophe. Development of the base game is done under open collaboration, with some game servers forking and modifying this code under separate licenses.

The game features the characters from the Puyo Puyo series, and also featured guest characters from several Japanese franchises like Detective Conan, Sailor Moon, and My Melody.

Android:room-two.d: The Room Two is a 2013 puzzle video game developed by British-based Fireproof Games as a sequel to The Room. The game was originally developed for the iPad and released in December 2013; it was made universal to work with the iPhone in January 2014. The Android version was released in February 2014. A Windows version was released on 5 July 2016.
